rejected_claims.reason: The lambda = 0.3 -> 0.7 strategy and the 'sampling'/'reinforcing' phrasing rest solely on the Codex run's own answer text echoed as an evidence passage; Codex opened no URLs and no tool payload is supplied. The second supplied run fetched the same PDF (and the CMU mirror) and reports it is a scanned image with no extractable text layer, explicitly warning: 'Treat any specific lambda recommendation attributed to Carbonell & Goldstein as unverified here.' The pattern '0\.3 .* 0\.7' is also loose enough to match unrelated numbers.

The Reuters reranking narrative (duplicate pushed down, 'novel but still relevant' moved up, similar documents demoted) has no corroboration anywhere in the supplied evidence outside the Codex answer echo, and the source PDF is reported unreadable by the other run. The patterns are also exact-phrase matches ('Reuters reranking example', 'duplicate article .* pushed down') that a correct, well-sourced response need not reproduce, making them overly narrow for lexical grading.

Only the existence of a user preference study favoring MMR is corroborated (the second run, from indexed summaries, notes 'a majority preferred the MMR ordering' but states 'the study's size and statistical treatment are unknown to me'). The distinguishing specifics graded by the patterns - 5 undergraduate users, 9 search tasks, lambda = 0.5, 4 of 5, and the 'too small for statistically significant' caveat - come only from the Codex answer echo attributed to a PDF the other run found to have no text layer.

The four ERR-IA figures (0.1913/0.2022, 0.2436/0.2735, 0.4172/0.4284) and the MMRlist-vs-ListMLE comparison are attributed to a course-page PDF (dmice.ohsu.edu/.../zhu_2014.pdf) that no supplied run opened and that appears nowhere in the second run's results. Nothing in the supplied evidence independently attests these numbers, and the second run's TREC-based findings point the other way, so this reads as invented benchmark detail.

The cited source (ambuehler.ethz.ch/CDstore/www2010/www/p881.pdf) was never opened by either run and appears nowhere in the second run's retrieved results, so the figures 0.186 -> 0.150 and 0.071 -> 0.058 are unverified. The independently corroborated finding is materially weaker - 'at best marginal yet not significant improvements' and MMR being 'least effective' - so 'MMR hurt the original ranking' plus the superlative 'only approach that consistently improved all three baseline rankers' overstates the contradictory evidence while grading on unverified decimals.
